text_block_list.name: Taiki Shuttle
text_block_list.text: Howdy, Flower! Please teach me a Japanese proverb!

text_block_list.name: Taiki Shuttle
text_block_list.text:
What does 'Today wa Motocross' mean? Grass said it 
just now.

text_block_list.name: Nishino Flower
text_block_list.text:
Um, I think... it’s actually 'Even the base of a 
lighthouse is dark,' right?

text_block_list.name: Nishino Flower
text_block_list.text:
The meaning is... 'Things close at hand are actually 
hard to see.' Because they get hidden in the shadow 
at your feet.

text_block_list.name: Taiki Shuttle
text_block_list.text: Ohh, shadow! In that case, I know a similar proverb!

text_block_list.name: Taiki Shuttle
text_block_list.text:
'If you lean, lean on Taiki’s shade!' Does that one 
mean the same?

text_block_list.name: Nishino Flower
text_block_list.text:
That proverb means 'If you rely on something, rely 
on something strong and great.' So it’s a little 
different.

text_block_list.name: Nishino Flower
text_block_list.text: And the reading isn't Taiki, it's 'taiju' (big tree)

text_block_list.name: Taiki Shuttle
text_block_list.text: I see... I made a mistake...

text_block_list.name: Nishino Flower
text_block_list.text: Fufu, the reading might be wrong, but...

text_block_list.name: Nishino Flower
text_block_list.text:
The meaning surely fits. That’s what I always think. 
If I ever have to rely on someone... it would be 
you, Senior Taiki.
